evals.prompt: we're adding a 'redeem lead' button to our partner portal (Next.js + Playwright, partners have owner/admin/viewer roles, redeeming spends the partner's prepaid budget). the repo has ~60 playwright specs but no e2e/journeys.md or anything like it. what should I do first, and what should the e2e coverage for redeem look like? give me the concrete plan, not theory.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the journey inventory by audience/persona first; redeem is T1 (money); lists lifecycle + refusal states (over budget, closed booking, viewer refused) with how to force them; defect to put back; journey row in the same PR.
assertions: Says to create/draft e2e/journeys.md before writing new specs
Groups journeys by audience or persona (partner roles named)
Classifies redeem as the top tier (T1 or equivalent) because it moves money
Lists at least two refusal states (e.g. over budget, closed booking, viewer not allowed)
Says how to reach states deterministically (factory/seed data, clock, or route) rather than walking the UI
Requires proving the test can fail (put the defect back / mutation)
Says the feature's journey row is added or updated in the same PR
Uses copy keys / catalogue lookups rather than hardcoded button text

evals.prompt:
this keeps flaking on CI, can you fix it and explain what's wrong?

```ts
test('save webinar', async ({ operatorPage: page }) => {
  await page.goto('/webinars/new')
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click()   // sometimes does nothing at all
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000)
  expect(await page.getByText('Saved').isVisible()).toBe(true)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export' }).click()
  const res = await page.waitForResponse('**/api/export')
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200)
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')
})
```
Next.js app router, playwright 1.5x. retries are set to 2 on CI.
evals.expected_output: Removes waitForTimeout/networkidle; web-first assertion on the toast; waitForResponse started before click; diagnoses the lost click as hydration and fixes it with an app readiness marker in the fixture; retries 1 + failOnFlakyTests; copy via keys.
assertions: Removes waitForTimeout and replaces it with a web-first assertion (await expect(...).toBeVisible/toHaveText)
Removes or rejects waitForLoadState('networkidle')
Starts waitForResponse (or the download/response promise) before the click
Identifies the lost click as a hydration race
Proposes an app-published readiness signal (e.g. data-hydrated) asserted once in a fixture, not force:true or a sleep
Recommends fewer retries and/or failOnFlakyTests so flakes fail instead of hiding
Does not recommend force: true or raising timeouts as the fix

evals.prompt: design renamed our colour tokens and changed the selected-row colour, and now 14 e2e tests fail on stuff like `await expect(row).toHaveClass(/bg-primary-100/)` and `toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(237, 233, 254)')`. same week marketing changed 'Save changes' to 'Save' and 9 more broke. how do we fix these so a redesign or copy edit doesn't break the suite again? we're EN + DE with next-intl.
evals.expected_output: State via ARIA first (aria-selected), paint via resolved token not hex/class, contrast ratio, screenshots last; copy via t('key') from the real catalogue with a throwing helper and lint; one locale end to end; key renames fail loudly.
assertions: Says to stop asserting class names
Recommends asserting selection through ARIA state (aria-selected / aria-current) first
Recommends comparing computed style against a resolved design token rather than a hex/rgb literal
Recommends resolving visible strings from the next-intl catalogue by key (t('...')) instead of literals, including name: in getByRole
Mentions enforcement (lint rule or a helper that throws on a missing key)
Keeps screenshots/visual diffs as a last resort rather than the main fix
